title: reading-notes-llm-inference-amelia-park
content:
Reading notes / scratchpad: LLM inference optimizations and recent papers (quick summaries + action items)

Context: personal notes while skimming papers and blog posts relevant to Redwood runtime improvements (batching, KV cache strategy, quantization profiles, speculative decoding). Mostly brain-dump; use as checklist for experiments.

1) FlashAttention 2 / attention kernel improvements (paper + blog)
- Key idea: fused kernels for attention that reduce memory bandwidth and enable longer context with lower overhead.
- Takeaways: huge perf wins for long-seq use cases; need careful kernel selection per hardware.
- Relevance to Redwood: integrate heuristic to choose FlashAttention-like kernel when seq_len > threshold and GPU supports it.
- Notes to self: measure latency vs throughput crossover on A100 vs H100 for seq lengths 1024/2048/4096. Add microbench harness.

2) Speculative Decoding (blog + paper variants)
- Idea: run a cheap draft model to propose tokens, verify with expensive model; can reduce token cost while keeping quality.
- Pitfalls: hallucination risk and verification overhead; complexity in streaming APIs.
- Relevance: could be an optional pipeline for Dedicated customers who want cost savings with configurable risk.
- Quick experiment idea: use small decoder-only 7B as draft + 34B as verifier. Measure token savings and added tail latency.

3) 4-bit Quantization & GPTQ-like approaches
- Several recent works show post-training quant (GPTQ, AWQ) can fit large models in 4-bit with acceptable quality.
- Practical issues: calibration time, codegen for kernels, per-channel vs per-tensor scaling.
- Relevance: big win for Dedicated/private deployments — lower memory footprint -> higher packing density.
- Action: schedule eval run converting Llama-weights to 4-bit with current toolchain; compare perplexity and generation quality on Redwood eval set.

4) KV-cache management and prefix caching strategies
- Papers/blogs highlight saving KV across sessions for identical prefixes and checkpointing for streaming.
- Redwood-specific thought: expose TTL and cache-key policies per route; use lightweight LRU + fingerprinting for common system prompts.
- Experiment: measure hit rate for STT/chatbot workloads; simulate time-based invalidation.

5) Batching and dynamic batching policies (workload-aware batching)
- Key tradeoffs: latency SLO vs token throughput. Dynamic batching that adapts to latency percentiles is best.
- Implementation note: maintain separate queues per route/tier; consider predictive batching for expected short requests (use small window).
- To test: run synthetic mix (50% short 8-token, 30% medium 64-token, 20% long 512-token) and evaluate average latency and p95 under different batching policies.

6) Streaming + early-token heuristics
- For interactive apps, partial-token streaming matters more than mean latency. Some ideas: prioritize streaming first N tokens ASAP by bypassing heavy verification, then validate later.
- Caveat: must ensure user-visible consistency; document behavior for SDKs.

7) Benchmarking and eval methodology reminders
- Use consistent prompt sets (reuse Redwood eval prompt suite). Track relative cost per token (including GPU time + infra overhead).
- Capture token-level latency breakdown (model compute, queuing, network, serialization).
- Add metric: gen-quality delta vs baseline (BLEU/ROUGE/LLMScore/embedding-sim).

Open questions / TODO
- Which quant toolchain is least effort to integrate into our inference path? (GPTQ vs AWQ vs custom kernels)
- How to expose speculative-decoding as first-class feature in API/console? Pricing model? safety controls?
- Where to add cache TTL knobs in console for per-route control? UX for customers to understand correctness tradeoffs.

Short-term experiments (next 6 weeks)
- Microbench: FlashAttention vs baseline on H100/A100 for seq 512/1024/2048. (owner: me)
- Quant test: convert small Llama 13B -> 4-bit, evaluate perplexity and ppl on eval-1000 prompts. (owner: Samira)
- SpecDec prototype: draft+verify pipeline on internal harness; measure cost savings and tail latency. (owner: Noah)
- Batching sim: run mixed-workload sim, tune batch windows and per-route queues. (owner: me)

Random notes to self (fragments)
- Remember to check memory fragmentation when packing multiple quantized models on same GPU.
- Could use cheap LM to classify requests into short/long to drive scheduling.
- Add telemetry: record model-variant used (fp16/4bit/specdec) per request for cost attribution.

References & links (for quick copy)
- FlashAttention: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14105
- Speculative Decoding overview: blog posts + recent papers (search arXiv 2023-2025)
- GPTQ/AWQ repos: GitHub -> GPTQ-for-LLaMa / AWQ repo
- Internal: CONFLUENCE:INF-optimizations-2025, JIRA:INF-321

End of notes. Keep short bullets. Will iterate and move to a proper PRD once initial benchmark numbers land.

Status: draft — for my eyes & quick share with Noa/Samira for experiment coordination.
